ORCHESTRATOR_VERIFICATION_FAILURE.root_cause: The orchestrator ran `bun run lint` REPO-WIDE and grepped stdout for a `path:line:col rule` pattern. Two independent defects made that check structurally blind: (1) Biome caps printed diagnostics (default --max-diagnostics=20) and this run's own .sdlc JSON format errors crowded out the source diagnostics; (2) Biome emits `format` diagnostics as `path format ---` with NO :line:col, so the grep pattern could never match a format error at all.
ORCHESTRATOR_VERIFICATION_FAILURE.why_it_matters: A gate reported as met while objectively failed is worse than the diagnostics. It means the run's self-verification did not run the check it claimed to.
ORCHESTRATOR_VERIFICATION_FAILURE.lesson: Scope the linter to the paths under test and raise --max-diagnostics; never infer a gate result from a grep over truncated repo-wide output.
ORCHESTRATOR_VERIFICATION_FAILURE.resolution: All 12 diagnostics fixed via Edit (not biome --write, per the run's Bash-read-only rule). Re-verified: `Checked 79 files` with zero diagnostics.

invariants.performed_by: main session, Playwright against `bun run dev:web`, local/anonymous mode
invariants.week: VERIFIED. Registry attributes render; click targeting resolves; timed drag moves (y 367->494); cross-column drag moves (x 576->739); endDate resize grows without moving (h 118->223, dy=0).
invariants.day: VERIFIED. Click opens the form; timed drag moves (y 133->175); endDate resize works on a 'Focus block' card (h 201->303, dy=0).
invariants.verdict: No regression attributable to CMP-104. Every interaction exercised behaves correctly on BOTH views, resize included.
invariants.coverage_gap_CORRECTED: An earlier version of this entry said Day's endDate resize was unexercisable. THAT WAS WRONG - it works on 4 of 6 Day cards and was demonstrated live. The real gap is different and applies to BOTH views: NEITHER VIEW HAS ANY TEST ASSERTING THAT A POINTER CAN ACTUALLY REACH A RESIZE HANDLE, on any card. The suite exercises resize at the adapter level by synthesising events on the handle element directly, which cannot observe occlusion - which is exactly why a defect affecting ~30% of cards in both views was invisible to 2309 passing tests and only surfaced under a real pointer.

invariants.name: BOTH views: endDate resize handle is occluded on ~30% of event cards - PRE-EXISTING product defect
invariants.severity: real product defect affecting BOTH views at a similar rate; found by manual verification, invisible to the test suite
invariants.SCOPE_CORRECTED: This finding was FIRST RECORDED AS DAY-SPECIFIC AND THAT WAS WRONG. The original characterisation came from sampling ONE card per view. Re-characterised by enumerating EVERY timed card in both views and probing elementFromPoint at each endDate handle centre. It is not view-specific and Day-vs-Week asymmetries cannot explain it.
invariants.observed: On affected cards the endDate resize handle exists in the DOM at the expected coordinates but elementFromPoint at its own centre does not return it, so the gesture falls through to the card body and degrades SILENTLY INTO A MOVE (first sampled instance: h 56->53, y 172->213). MEASURED MATRIX (demo seed, viewport 1500x950): WEEK 12 of 17 cards reachable - unreachable are 'Morning standup' (h=25), 'Gym' (h=40), 'Try Compass' (h=54), 'Design review' (h=54), 'Design review 10 - 11 AM' (h=54). DAY 4 of 6 reachable - unreachable are 'Morning standup' (h=25), 'Try Compass' (h=52). Roughly 30% of cards in each view.
invariants.NOT_height_dependent: Height is not the discriminator, which rules out the other obvious shape. At h=54 in Week, 'Exercise', 'Call a friend', 'Lunch with Sam', 'Dentist' and 'Team sync' all REACH the handle while 'Try Compass' and 'Design review' do NOT.
invariants.pre_existing_PROVEN_not_inferred: The main session stashed this run's changes, confirmed the tree was back to the 795/607 baseline, re-ran the FULL MATRIX against main@2d81253a, and reproduced BYTE-IDENTICAL results - same cards, same blockers, in both views. It then restored and verified git status matched the pre-stash snapshot exactly with the adapters back at 494/306.
structural_corroboration_verified_by_orc: git status --porcelain on packages/web/src/grid/interaction/dom.ts and packages/web/src/grid/components/ is EMPTY - neither the handle attribute definition nor the card that renders it was touched by this run.
All 36 changed paths are inside the three allowlisted directories.
invariants.MECHANISM_UNCONFIRMED: The framing initially suggested at close-out - 'the handle is nested inside data-calendar-event-content rather than being a card-root sibling as in Week' - does NOT survive a read of the source and must not be carried into the ticket. There is ONE shared card, grid/components/TimedEventCard.tsx, used by both views (Week via views/Week/components/Event/Grid/GridEvent/GridEvent.tsx, Day via views/Day/components/Calendar/DayCalendarEventCards.tsx). Both resize handles are nested inside the EVENT_CONTENT_ATTRIBUTE div at lines 342 and 353 for BOTH views, so handle nesting cannot be the difference. showResizeCursor is likewise computed identically for both at line 232 (!isPlaceholder && !isResizing && !isDragging).
invariants.onScalerMouseDown_asymmetry_DEMOTED_from: RECORDED AS A VERIFIED FACT ABOUT THE CODE, NOT AS A CANDIDATE CAUSE. Week passes onScalerMouseDown to the shared card (GridEvent.tsx:146, GridDraft.tsx:159/178); Day never does (absent from DayCalendarEventCards.tsx:180). It was briefly the leading candidate while the defect was believed Day-specific. It CANNOT be the cause: the defect affects WEEK at the same ~30% rate, so no Day-vs-Week asymmetry can explain it. It was independently already insufficient anyway, being optional-chained at TimedEventCard.tsx:346,357.
invariants.OBSERVATION_not_mechanism_blockers: document.elementsFromPoint() at an occluded handle's centre returns a stack topped by LAYOUT CONTAINERS, with the card and its handle absent entirely. Observed blockers: div.relative.ml-[50px].h-full.w-full, div.absolute.top-0.left-12.5.grid, div.flex.h-12.w-full.shrink-0 - and in the first Day sample, all-day-row elements (data-all-day-tint). The discriminator is therefore WHICH CARDS GET OVERLAPPED BY GRID CHROME, probably a function of overlap/deck layout position rather than of the card itself. This is a LEAD, NOT a mechanism: it says what is on top, not why the handle is beneath it. MECHANISM REMAINS UNCONFIRMED and no further candidate is being proposed.
invariants.rejected_candidate_showResizeCursor: showResizeCursor was nearly proposed as the cause on the strength of the probe measuring cursor:auto in Day vs row-resize in Week. IT DOES NOT HOLD, and is recorded so nobody re-derives it: showResizeCursor = !isPlaceholder && !isResizing && !isDragging (TimedEventCard.tsx:232) contains nothing view-specific, and the measured cursor:auto belonged to the element elementFromPoint RETURNED - the coverer - not to the handle. Caught before it was written into the ticket.

invariants.first_of_its_kind: FIRST arm on the Antigravity SDK door (flash-agsdk-worker).
invariants.isolates: Arm 2 (20260824-002919-refactor-week-day-interaction) ran the SAME policy name, opus-plus-flash-v37, on the flash-COMPLETION door. This pair therefore isolates the DOOR, not the policy.

invariants.independence_of_this_arm: Branch cut fresh from main@2d81253a. Discovery was forbidden from reading any prior arm's artifacts and re-derived the duplication table from the working tree alone; the pre-refactor LOC fingerprint 795/607/149/149 was verified intact before work began.
supported_findings: Refactor task types never reach the mechanical tier under this policy: refactor_extract/patch_apply are absent from the codegen rule's task_type list, so 13 of 18 codegen packets fell to default:opus and only the 5 tests-phase packets hit Flash. On a refactor ticket this policy is effectively single-tier, and the tier split is a function of ticket type, not policy.

The SDK door cannot write cross-directory test files without surrendering its sandbox. The worker was correctly denied twice (packages/web/package.json, packages/web/src), but a test needing simultaneous imports from grid/interaction and both views has no viable narrow work_dir.
The worker's returned payload is not a reliable record of what it wrote (one response carried injected CJK mid-token while the file on disk was clean ASCII).
It rewrites whole files when asked to append - survivable only because every test-name set was diffed against HEAD.
A worker denied a read guesses rather than fails; the guessed ownership-reason strings happened to be correct.
invariants.unsupported_axis: COST. This arm is auth_mode=estimated, books input_tokens_cached=0 and materially overstates real claude-cli billing; the premium half is heuristic while the Flash half is vendor-reported. The ~$25 total must not be quoted as a policy comparison and influenced no technical decision.
